coaches.name: Cliff Meredith
coaches.summary: Cliff Meredith is a member of the Mid-Valley USBC Hall of Fame. He bowled in college for Linn-Benton Community College and Oregon State University, including USBC sectional competition, and he coached the Central Oregon Community College team while working at Sun Mountain Lanes. He has led youth programs in the Albany area, coached South Albany High School bowling for three years, and served eight years as the Oregon State USBC high school manager. He has also worked with the University of Oregon and Oregon State University on their college bowling programs. He is a USBC registered volunteer and has completed SafeSport certification. He wants bowling to feel welcoming both for athletes who compete and for those who bowl because they enjoy it.

coaches.name: Chris Breshears
coaches.summary: Chris Breshears is from Albany and has been bowling since 1994, starting in the youth program at B & D Bowl. He has competed across the country, bowled for West Albany High School, and in 1998 helped restart the high school program while he was still a bowler. After graduation he coached the boys’ and girls’ teams for several years and coached youth leagues in the Albany area. He is certified in bowling ball drilling and fitting. His focus is giving back to young bowlers in the community.

intro: Albany High School Bowling teaches the game and helps student athletes grow into it. The aim is skill, confidence, teamwork, and sportsmanship.
club.coachesNote: Biographies below are summarized from the club’s current website.

teamSport.heading: A team sport
paragraphs: Practices build individual form, and tournaments turn that work into a shared score. The club uses Baker format, where five bowlers complete one game together. You do not have to carry every frame by yourself.
bullets: Bowling is both an individual skill and a team sport.
During practices, students develop their approach, release, accuracy, and consistency.
In Baker format, five bowlers share a single ten-frame game.
In a standard five-bowler Baker lineup, bowlers take assigned frames, commonly 1 and 6, 2 and 7, 3 and 8, 4 and 9, and 5 and 10.
Team members contribute to one combined score.
Encouragement, cooperation, focus, and sportsmanship are important.
teamSport.lineupNote: Coaches determine the actual competition lineups and procedures.

volunteers.heading: Volunteers make it possible
paragraphs: The club depends on parents, families, and community members who support our existing athletes. Adults can help with tournaments, fundraising, setup, general club needs, and transportation when additional approval is granted.
bullets: Coaches teach approach, aiming, balance, release, scoring, and team bowling.
Bowling helps student athletes build confidence, friendships, patience, and teamwork.
Athletes on the roster can chase competitive scores or enjoy the game with teammates.
Adult volunteers help keep practices, events, and fundraisers running.
Background screening for volunteers uses Sterling Volunteers when leadership directs it.

college.heading: College bowling opportunities
college.intro: Some athletes continue on to college bowling. Ask a coach what that path looks like. The club can point you to current information.
bullets: Bowling can continue beyond high school.
Some colleges offer bowling teams or collegiate bowling programs.
Opportunities and participation requirements vary by institution.
Students interested in collegiate bowling can speak with coaches about developing skills, tracking progress, and exploring programs.
Scholarship opportunities and eligibility depend on individual programs and applicable requirements.
college.disclaimer: These USBC pages are general learning resources. They do not promise a scholarship, a roster spot, or eligibility.

volunteer.title: Volunteer With Albany High School Bowling
intro: The Albany High School Bowling Club depends on the generosity of parents, families, and community members who help make our bowling program possible.
volunteer.waysIntro: Volunteer roles support the athletes already on the roster. Availability and approval depend on club needs and applicable school procedures.
opportunities: Student transportation, subject to additional approval
screeningParagraphs: Albany High School Bowling uses Sterling Volunteers as its preferred third-party background-screening provider for adult volunteers. Screening helps protect student athletes and supports safe club activities.

This website does not collect sensitive personal information for background checks, and it does not process screening applications. Screening is handled through Sterling Volunteers and any school or club procedures that leadership confirms.
volunteer.screeningNotice: Contact club leadership before you order a background check. Completing a screening does not mean you are automatically authorized to volunteer with the club.
volunteer.screeningMissing: An organization-specific Sterling Volunteers invitation link has not been published here yet. Use the informational link below to learn about Sterling Volunteers, then email club leadership for current screening instructions.
volunteer.screeningReady: Use the club’s Sterling Volunteers invitation link only after leadership confirms you should begin screening for a volunteer role.
transportParagraphs: Helping with student transportation is separate from general volunteer screening. Adults interested in driving or otherwise supporting travel for athletes may need additional authorization beyond a standard volunteer background check.
This site does not claim that a standard Sterling Volunteers package includes a motor vehicle record (MVR) review, and it does not claim that any transportation requirements are already satisfied.
volunteer.transportListIntro: Requirements for transportation help may include:
transportItems: A motor vehicle record (MVR) review, when required by the school or club
Written authorization from club leadership and any applicable school or district procedures
volunteer.transportClosing: Ask club leadership what is currently required before offering rides or arranging student transportation.
